title: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n grid, each cell contains a sign directing you to another cell: 1 for right, 2 for left, 3 for down, 4 for up.
statement: Given an m x n grid, each cell contains a sign directing you to another cell: 1 for right, 2 for left, 3 for down, 4 for up. Starting from the top-left cell (0,0), you must reach the bottom-right cell (m-1, n-1) following these signs. If a sign points outside the grid, it is invalid. You can change the sign of any cell once, with a cost of 1, to make at least one valid path from the start to the end. The task is to determine the minimum cost required to ensure such a path exists.
constraints: Cell values one, two, three, and four point right, left, down, and up respectively.
Moving in the indicated direction costs zero; choosing any other direction means changing that cell and costs one.
Return the minimum cost of a path from top-left to bottom-right.
hints: Treat each cell as a graph node with outgoing edge weights zero or one.
Use a deque: zero-cost moves go to the front and changed-sign moves go to the back.
Relax a neighbor only when its new cost improves the stored distance.
Zero-one BFS processes these binary-weight edges in nondecreasing distance like Dijkstra without a heap.
editorial: The four possible outgoing moves have cost zero for the cell’s current arrow and one otherwise. A 0–1 BFS pushes zero edges to the deque front and one edges to the back while applying ordinary distance relaxation. The oracle independently uses heap-based Dijkstra on seeded grids.

tests.explanation: Following each row and changing direction between rows costs three.
The signs already permit a zero-cost route to the destination.
